title: Pointed finite-groupoid etale neighbourhoods of finite-inertia DM stacks
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Stacks in groupoids, Deligne--Mumford stacks, representability by algebraic spaces, and 2-fibre products have the meanings in [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids, def-trf-algebraic-space]. For a stack $\mathcal A$, its inertia $I_{\mathcal A}(T)$ has objects $(a,\alpha)$ with $a\in\mathcal A(T)$ and $\alpha\in\operatorname{Aut}(a)$, and arrows $v:(a,\alpha)\to(b,\beta)$ with $v\alpha=\beta v$. The projection forgets $\alpha$. Finite inertia means that every scheme base change of this projection is a scheme finite over its base [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]. The point space $|\mathcal A|$ consists of field-valued objects modulo isomorphism after common field extension, with topology detected by a scheme atlas. A geometric stabilizer at a point is the automorphism group algebraic space of a representative over an algebraically closed field; comparison means comparison after a common algebraically closed field extension. Let $\mathcal X/S$ be Deligne--Mumford with finite inertia and let $x\in|\mathcal X|$. There are affine $S$-schemes $U,R$, a groupoid scheme $(U,R,s,t,e,i,c)$ [def-a1-groupoid-scheme] over $S$ with $s,t$ finite locally free [def-pc-finite-locally-free], a Deligne--Mumford stack $\mathcal Q/S$ identified with $[U/R]$, a representable-by-algebraic-spaces etale map $g:\mathcal Q\to\mathcal X$, and $q\in|\mathcal Q|$ with $g(q)=x$, such that the induced map of geometric stabilizer group algebraic spaces at $q$ and $x$ is an isomorphism. Here $[U/R]$ is the fppf stackification of the groupoid of $U(T)$-objects and $R(T)$-arrows [def-pc-fppf-site, lem-sfb-groupoid-stackification-local-description]; etale means [def-weil-etale-morphism] on scheme charts. No assertion of stabilizer preservation away from $q$ is made.

source.place: Tag 0DU4 (lemma-etale-local-quasi-DM-at-x), specialized to Deligne--Mumford stacks with finite inertia; Tag 06N3 (theorem-DM) for DM permanence under representable etale maps. The finite inertia hypothesis gives the quasi-DM separated-diagonal hypothesis of 0DU4 via Tag 0CL0 (lemma-diagonal-diagonal).

proof.text: Choose a surjective etale scheme atlas $A\to\mathcal X$ and a point over $x$, using the Deligne--Mumford definition. An affine open $V\subseteq A$ containing that point exists by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-opens-basis]. The open immersion $V\to A$ is etale by [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-etale], and its composite $a:V\to\mathcal X$ is etale by [lem-sfb-stack-chartwise-smooth-etale-calculus]. Apply [lem-sfb-dm-finite-inertia-affine-relation] to $a$. Thus $R=V\times_{\mathcal X}V$ is a scheme groupoid with separated, flat, locally finitely presented, locally quasi-finite projections and finite stabilizer at the chosen point $v$. No quasi-compactness of $\mathcal X$ or separatedness of $S$ is needed.

source.place: Tag 0DU4 (lemma-etale-local-quasi-DM-at-x), first paragraph via 0DU3 (lemma-etale-local-quasi-DM), initial presentation.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-etale-groupoid-affine-stabilizer-splitting] to $(V,R,v)$. Obtain an affine etale $h:V'\to V$, a point $v'$ over $v$ with the same residue field, and an open wide subgroupoid $P\subseteq R'=R\times_{V\times_S V}(V'\times_S V')$ whose projections are finite locally free and which contains the whole stabilizer fibre at $v'$. The composite $a'=a h$ is etale by the chart calculus. The identification $R'=V'\times_{\mathcal X}V'$ sends an arrow $r$ and its two specified lifts to the same isomorphism $a(h(v'_1))\simeq a(h(v'_2))$; the inverse forgets the lifts into $V$ and retains the two points of $V'$. These inverse operations respect composition and pullback, so this is an identification of the actual self-relation groupoids, not just point sets.

source.place: Tag 0DU4, affine etale splitting and self-relation identification; spaces-more-groupoids.tex Tag 0DTE (lemma-splitting-affine-scheme).

proof.text: Apply the affine-relation node to $a':V'\to\mathcal X$: its quotient $[V'/R']$ is a Deligne--Mumford open substack of $\mathcal X$. By [lem-sfb-open-subgroupoid-etale-quotient], $\mathcal Q=[V'/P]$ is Deligne--Mumford and $\mathcal Q\to[V'/R']$ is representable etale. Composing with that open immersion gives the required representable etale $g:\mathcal Q\to\mathcal X$, by the chart calculus. Both object and arrow schemes are affine: $V'$ was chosen affine, and $P$ is affine because it is finite over $V'$ by [def-pc-finite-locally-free] and [lem-weil-pbc-finite-morphism-permanence](b). Use $U=V'$, $R_{\mathrm{out}}=P$ for the groupoid in the conclusion.

source.place: Tag 0DU4, application of 0DU2 (lemma-quasi-splitting-etale) and conclusion; DM consequence of 06N3 (theorem-DM).

proof.text: Let $q$ be the image of $v'$ in $[V'/P]$; its image in $\mathcal X$ is $x$, since $h(v')=v$ and $a(v)$ represents $x$. By [lem-sfb-fppf-groupoid-stack-presentations](1), the self-relation of $V'\to[V'/P]$ is exactly $P$, so the automorphism group scheme of the object given by $v'$ over $\kappa(v')$ is the fibre of $P$ along $(v',v')$. By [lem-sfb-dm-finite-inertia-affine-relation] applied to $a'$, with $V'\times_{\mathcal X}V'=R'$ from step 2, the automorphism group scheme of $a'(v')$ in $\mathcal X$ is the stabilizer fibre $G'_{v'}$ of $R'$ along $(v',v')$. The composite $V'\to\mathcal Q\to\mathcal X$ is $a'$, and arrows of $\mathcal Q$ map through the inclusion $P\subseteq R'$; so the map induced by $g$ is the inclusion of the $P$-fibre into $G'_{v'}$, i.e. the restriction of $G'_{v'}$ to the open $P$. The splitting contains every point of $G'_{v'}$, so this open restriction is the entire scheme, with the same restricted structure sheaf. The inclusion therefore induces an isomorphism of stabilizer schemes preserving multiplication, identity and inverse. Base change to an algebraic closure gives the stated isomorphism of geometric stabilizer group algebraic spaces. This argument uses no information about stabilizers at other points.

source.place: Tag 0DU4, final sentence: the splitting contains the stabilizer; spaces-groupoids.tex Tag 04M9 (lemma-quotient-stack-2-cartesian).

lean.statement: theorem exists_dm_pointed_finite_groupoid_neighbourhood {S : Scheme.{u}} (X : BasedCategory.{v, w} (Over S)) (hX : IsDeligneMumfordModuliStack X) (hfinite : IsRepresentableFiniteModuliMap (moduliInertiaProjection X)) (x : ModuliPoints X) : ∃ (U R : Over S) (s t : R ⟶ U) (e : U.left ⟶ R.left) (i : R.left ⟶ R.left) (c : pullback s.left t.left ⟶ R.left), IsAffine U.left ∧ IsAffine R.left ∧ IsGroupoidScheme s.left t.left e i c ∧ s.left.IsFiniteLocallyFree ∧ t.left.IsFiniteLocallyFree ∧ ∃ (Q : BasedCategory.{max u v, max (u + 1) w} (Over S)) (a : BasedFunctor (discreteModuli (yoneda.obj U)) Q), Nonempty (SchemeGroupoidQuotientPresentation s t e i c Q a) ∧ IsDeligneMumfordModuliStack Q ∧ ∃ (g : BasedFunctor Q X) (q : ModuliPoints Q), IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces g ∧ IsEtaleModuliMap g ∧ moduliPointMap g q = x ∧ q ∈ moduliStabilizerIsomorphismLocus g
lean.note: Uses the existing fppf quotient-presentation, field-point quotient, inertia projection, finite scheme-test and geometric-stabilizer-locus interfaces. Only the chosen point belongs to the stabilizer-isomorphism locus; no global stabilizer preservation or separatedness of S is assumed.
